newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Amnesty seeks UN rights chief who speaks out.
newsitem.headline: Amnesty seeks UN rights chief who speaks out.

text.p: Amnesty International said on Monday that departing U.N. High Commissioner for Human Rights Jose Ayala Lasso had "consistently failed" to speak out against abuses.
It urged the world body to choose a successor who would do better.

In a statement, the London-based human rights organisation also urged member states to better finance U.N. field operations which now employ 250 rights monitors in 12 states, including Bosnia, Cambodia, Rwanda and Zaire.
U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan is expected to appoint a successor next month to Ayala Lasso, who left in March to become Ecuadoran Foreign Minister.

"The new High Commissioner must be willing to confront governments when necessary," Amnesty said in a 12-page statement issued in Geneva, where the U.N. Human Rights Commission winds up its annual six-week session on Friday.

Annan is known to prefer a woman for the post. Irish President Mary Robinson, nominated by her country for the job when she ends her presidency at year-end, and Sonia Picado, Costa Rica's ambassador to Washington, are known candidates.
Amnesty accused Ayala Lasso, whose office was created by the General Assembly in 1993, of having failed to meet expectations.
"Jose Ayala Lasso consistently failed to confront gross human rights violators," Amnesty said.

Shortcomings of what Amnesty termed Ayala Lasso's "quiet diplomacy" included his failure to speak out against repressive regimes and stalled attempts to open offices in Chechnya and Indonesia, the rights' group said.
But some U.N. sources defended Ayala Lasso, saying his quiet diplomacy had enabled the United Nations to set up vital rights monitoring offices in Rwanda, Burundi and Colombia.
"It was not quiet diplomacy for the sake of quiet diplomacy," said one U.N. source. "It achieved concrete results.

"We never would have had these critical (field) reports from Burundi and Rwanda -- which not even Amnesty can match -- if the High Commissioner had not started quiet diplomacy with those governments and made it possible to establish those offices."
